2.0.0.en: 1 Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds! when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand. 2 And they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away: so they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage. 3 Therefore thus saith the LORD; "Behold, against this family do I devise an evil, from which ye shall not remove your necks; neither shall ye go haughtily: for this time is evil.

2.0.1.en: Woe to them that devise iniquity, and work evil upon their beds!

2.0.2.en: When the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand. [1]

2.0.3.en: He pronounces woe upon those who stay awake at night planning, in selfishness, to seize what belongs to others, and when the morning comes they carry out what they had planned, because they are men of authority. All that occupies their thoughts and hearts is the coveting of what belongs to others, justifying this to themselves in one way or another. For example, a man reckons that he is more capable of managing and running the field, or that the owner of the field is unable to pay the debt whose interest has accumulated against him and swollen. With consummate skill they conspire how to fulfill the desire of their hearts. If injustice, seizure and covetousness are grave sins, they are graver still when a man devotes himself to arranging them, using his craftiness, his deceit, his resources and his authority! He thinks that no one has the right to call him to account.

2.0.4.en: It grieves the heart that wicked oppressors devote the night to planning evil and rise early with the light of morning to carry out what they have devised, while we are not occupied at night with prayer and meditation on the word of God, and do not rise early to work for the sake of the Kingdom of God. Therefore the wise man counsels us: "Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest" (Eccl 9:10).

2.0.5.en: What a man thinks about when he lies down for bodily rest reveals what is in his heart, his mind and his intentions. The spiritual man, when he lies down, has his soul lifted up to meditate on the joyful things of God, while the wicked man's soul is immersed in the evils that capture and enslave it. Moreover, just as the night reveals to us what we are by day, so what we think about by night leads to its being done by day, sooner or later. The holiness of our life by day gives us holy thoughts and dreams at night worthy of the children of God, and the holiness of our waking daydreams drives us still more toward spiritual growth in the Lord.

2.1.0.en: And they covet fields, and take them by violence; and houses, and take them away: so they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage. [2]

2.1.1.en: King Ahab was a wicked example of exploiting his authority according to the counsel of his wicked wife Jezebel (1 Kgs 21:1-15), when he took possession of the field of Naboth the Jezreelite after contriving his murder. This kind of corruption spread in Judah, and the nobles who held authority were struck with this grave disease.

2.1.2.en: * O rich man, why do you exalt yourself with your wealth and boast of the glories of your forefathers? Do you take pride in your homeland, and delight in the beauty of your body, and rejoice in a passing honor? Take heed to yourself. Remember that you are a mortal man, and that you are dust and to dust you shall return (Gen 3:19)... Bend down and look at the tombs: can you tell the bones of the poor from the bones of the rich? The bones of slaves from the bones of masters? Be mindful of yourself, then, and give up pride, miserliness and hardness of heart.

2.1.3.en: * You have become, O wealthy man, a servant of the all-merciful God and His steward before your brothers in servitude. So beware of thinking that these good things are for your belly. Reckon what is in your hands as something foreign to you. These goods charm you for a while, then soon evaporate and vanish, but you will give a strict account of them.

2.1.4.en: St. Basil the Great They seize the fields of others not only by craftiness and deceit, but by violence and tyranny, usurping the rights of others, against the law. They oppress the master of the house with no regard for his family or his inheritance from his forefathers.

2.2.0.en: Behold, against this family do I devise an evil, from which ye shall not remove your necks; neither shall ye go haughtily: for this time is evil. [3]

2.2.1.en: By the family he means here the whole kingdom, and by the evil he means here the chastening by captivity, which they see as an evil that has come upon them.

2.2.2.en: Yahweh repays these oppressors according to their deeds, and allows them the bonds of captivity from which their necks do not escape. Instead of their haughtiness their necks are encircled with fetters, and they are dragged to the land of captivity. Since the rich and the leaders placed a heavy yoke on the class of the peasants, He allows the heavy yoke of captivity to come upon them, and they cannot remove it from their necks; in this He breaks their pride and haughtiness.

2.3.0.en: 4 "In that day shall one take up a parable against you, and lament with a doleful lamentation, and say, We be utterly spoiled: he hath changed the portion of my people: how hath he removed it from me! turning away he hath divided our fields. 5 Therefore thou shalt have none that shall cast a cord by lot in the congregation of the LORD.

2.3.1.en: In that day shall one take up a parable against you, and lament with a doleful lamentation, and say:

2.3.3.en: He hath changed the portion of my people: how hath he removed it from me!

2.3.4.en: Turning away he hath divided our fields. [4]

2.3.5.en: As they plunder the possessions of others, they lose even their own possessions; the enemy takes over the fields, and seizes their lands and their harvests, so that they lose prosperity as well as the lands of their inheritance. They are torn away from them unexpectedly, and they are stunned because of the element of surprise and violence.

2.3.6.en: When the day of severe chastening comes, their joys are turned into laments, and their laughter into crying out, and they become a byword among their friends and neighbors.

2.3.7.en: * Thus this wretched soul is shaken (by covetousness), and the dragon of covetousness coils around it, and it cannot free itself, while it strives hard to multiply the heap of money which it has acquired by unlawful means and hateful diligence, accompanied by calamities that do not lessen the intensity of this soul's covetousness but increase its burning, and blind it to everything except running after gain and obtaining money... and stripping itself of faith, whenever it finds a glimmer of hope of obtaining money.

2.3.8.en: And for this reason he will not scruple to commit the crime of lying, or false witness, or theft, or breaking a promise, or giving way to wounding fits of rage. Also, if he loses hope of obtaining gain, he will not scruple to overstep the limits of propriety and humility, and in all this gold and the love of base profit become a god to him, like those who worship their bellies. For this reason the blessed Apostle, looking at the deadly poison of this plague, did not say only that it is the root of all evils, but also called it "idolatry," saying: "and covetousness, which is idolatry" (Col 3:5).

2.3.9.en: You see, then, the measure of the fall to which this madness leads step by step, so that the Apostle cries out loudly that it is the worship of false idols, because, overstepping the image and likeness of God (which every one who worships God in spirit and truth must keep in the depths of his soul without falsification), he has preferred to love and cling to the images engraved on gold instead of God.

2.3.10.en: By such great steps, going downward, he is driven from bad to worse, and finally he does not care to keep for himself, not the virtues of humility, love and obedience, nor even their shadow, besides becoming dissatisfied with everything, grumbling and complaining about every work. Then, having cast all reverence to the winds, like a runaway horse he rushes headlong with loosened reins.

2.3.11.en: * Do you wish to know how dangerous this temptation is, and its harm to its owner, unless it is uprooted with care, and the destruction it brings upon him, and the various branches of sins that spring from it? Look at Judas, who was numbered among the disciples, and consider how, because he did not move to crush the head of this deadly dragon, he was destroyed by its poison, and how, when he fell into the snare of this lust, it cast him into sin and into a swift fall, so that it seduced him to sell the Redeemer of mankind and the Author of man's salvation for thirty pieces of silver; and that it was not possible to drive him to this wicked sin, the sin of betraying his Master, unless he had been stained by the sin of covetousness. Nor would he have been driven to commit crime against his Master in such a hideous way unless he had accustomed himself to steal from the purse entrusted to him.

2.4.0.en: St. John Cassian Therefore thou shalt have none that shall cast a cord by lot in the congregation of the LORD. [5]

2.4.1.en: There will be no one to distribute the inheritance or to dispute over it, because all lose the inheritance; there is no need for disputes and courts and casting lots to divide the lands and fields, since everything passes into the hand of the seizing enemy. Their covetousness extends to everything: seizing fields, houses and inheritance, so that the peasants become destitute, with no shelter, deprived of the blessing of the inheritance of their fathers and forefathers.

2.4.2.en: God declares to the covetous that, since they unjustly rob the poor, what they have seized will be taken away from them, and they will even lose their money, so that they will have no portion in the land which God gave to His people.

2.5.s.en: 3. Their rejection of the word of prophecy:

2.5.2.en: They shall not prophesy concerning these things.

2.5.4.en: After speaking of the sin of covetousness and the sins that followed it, such as the devising of evil, injustice, seizure and haughtiness, he speaks of a grave sin, which is resisting the word of the Lord, for they demand that the mouths of the prophets be shut. They do not stop at rebelling against civil laws, but rebel also against the authority of God. The wicked cannot endure the word of the Lord, nor do they accept rebuke, so they asked the prophet to keep silent and cease prophesying, counting the word of the Lord as disgrace and shame. They see in the word of the Lord a disturbance and terror to their souls. Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, sent to Jeroboam king of Israel asking him to prevent Amos from prophesying (Amos 7:10 ff.). And it is written in Isaiah: "Which say to the seers, See not" (Isa 30:10). This behavior remains even to the age of the Antichrist, when those who dwell on the earth are tormented by the preaching of the word (Rev 11:10).

2.5.5.en: We often reject frankness in the guidance of our life, and ask for soft words and deceptive human consolations, though we are in need of firmness springing from love.

2.6.s.en: 4. The prophet does not keep silent:

2.6.0.en: 7 O thou that art named the house of Jacob, is the spirit of the LORD straitened? are these his doings? "do not my words do good to him that walketh uprightly? 8 Even of late my people is risen up as an enemy: ye pull off the robe with the garment from them that pass by securely as men averse from war. 9 The women of my people have ye cast out from their pleasant houses; from their children have ye taken away my glory for ever.

2.6.1.en: O thou that art named the house of Jacob, is the spirit of the LORD straitened?

2.6.3.en: Do not my words do good to him that walketh uprightly? [7]

2.6.4.en: He says: "O thou that art named the house of Jacob," for they bear the name but do not practice what befits their name. As the Apostle says: "Behold, thou art called a Jew, and restest in the law, and makest thy boast of God, and knowest his will, and approvest the things that are more excellent, being instructed out of the law; and art confident that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light of them which are in darkness, an instructor of the foolish, a teacher of babes, which hast the form of knowledge and of the truth in the law. Thou therefore which teachest another, teachest thou not thyself? thou that preachest a man should not steal, dost thou steal? thou that sayest a man should not commit adultery, dost thou commit adultery...?" (Rom 2:17-22).

2.6.5.en: The prophet did not keep silent as they asked him, but rebuked them, affirming to them that the secret of their disgrace is not his words but their conduct, which does not agree with the ways of the Lord, their life is not upright with the work of the Spirit of God. If it becomes upright, they receive the blessing of the Lord.

2.6.6.en: The prophet Micah rebukes them, saying: "Is the spirit of the LORD straitened?" meaning, do you think that you are able to silence the voice of the Lord and resist His Spirit? If you use every authority to silence the prophets, will the Spirit of God not find other ways to reprove you for your evil? Can your temporal authority and your material resources nullify the counsel of God?

2.6.7.en: And by his saying "Are these his doings?" he rebukes them, because they boast that they are the sons of Israel, the house of Jacob, and from them came the prophets. Did your father Jacob practice what you are doing? Do you walk in the same way as your father? You boast that you are the house of Jacob, but you do not do his works.

2.6.8.en: So also the Lord Christ rebuked the Jews when they boasted that they were the children of Abraham the free, while they wanted to kill the Lord Christ. Therefore He said to them: "If ye were Abraham's children, ye would do the works of Abraham. But now ye seek to kill me, a man that hath told you the truth, which I have heard of God: this did not Abraham. Ye do the deeds of your father... Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do" (Jn 8:39-44).

2.6.9.en: It is as though the prophet says to his people: You have the name "the house of Jacob," but your deeds testify that you are "the house of the devil, who resists the Spirit of the Lord."

2.6.10.en: If they wish to be ascribed to Jacob, who walked by the Spirit of the Lord, let them walk uprightly, as befits them.

2.6.11.en: St. Hippolytus of Rome sees that the house of Jacob provoked the wrath of God and was bound up with the sufferings of Christ according to the flesh.

2.6.12.en: * "And he was clothed with a vesture dipped in blood: and his name is called The Word of God" (Rev 19:13). See, then, my brethren, how the garment sprinkled with blood points to the flesh, through which the Word of God, who is not subject to suffering, endured suffering, as the prophet bears witness. For thus speaks the blessed Micah: "Must this be said, O house of Jacob? Is the spirit of the Lord short of patience? Are these his doings? Do not my words do good to him that walketh uprightly? But ye have risen up against my people as an enemy; ye strip the garment from the man of peace." This points to the sufferings of Christ in the flesh.

2.6.13.en: St. Hippolytus * Scripture is accustomed to call the priest an angel and a god, saying: "Thou shalt not revile the gods, nor curse the ruler of thy people." (Ex 22:28) LXX.

2.6.14.en: St. John Chrysostom * He who truly leaves this world and takes the yoke of Christ and learns from Him, and trains himself daily to bear toil, because the Lord is "meek and lowly in heart" (Mt 11:29), remains continually undisturbed by all trials, and for him "all things work together for good" (Rom 8:28). As the prophet (Micah) says, the words of God are good to him that walketh uprightly (Mic 2:7).

2.6.15.en: Abba Abraham Even of late my people is risen up as an enemy.

2.7.0.en: Ye pull off the robe with the garment from them that pass by securely as men averse from war. [8]

2.7.1.en: While they take pride in calling themselves "the house of Jacob" [7], they play the part of the enemy who shatters this house. They did not stand against the Spirit of the Lord only, but against the nation or the people as well, for in robbing the peasants they shatter "the house of Jacob," and are counted enemies resisting it. They are an internal enemy more dangerous than any external enemy.

2.7.2.en: The psalmist says: "For they speak not peace: but they devise deceitful matters against them that are quiet in the land" (Ps 35:20).

2.7.3.en: The hideousness of their conduct appears in that they not only rob the land, but even strip the robe from those who pass by securely, and from those whom they defended in battle.

2.7.4.en: The women of my people have ye cast out from their pleasant houses.

2.8.0.en: From their children have ye taken away my glory for ever. [9]

2.8.1.en: They devoured widows' houses (Mt 23:14), and took possession of them, and treated the women with a brutality inconsistent with humane conduct, especially since they were women of the same nation, women of the people of God, who seek God's protection for them.

2.8.2.en: Their hand stretched out to seize from the women their children to be slaves to them; perhaps they sold them as slaves to the pagan kingdoms, so that they deprived them of the enjoyment of faith in God, and stripped them of their glory.

2.8.3.en: Perhaps the prophet is pointing here to the captivity which God allowed because of the corruption and evil of the leaders, which spread among the people. For in captivity it does not stop at the seizing of women from their houses, but even the children lose their right to Hebrew nationality and to share in worship in the temple, as they are carried to a foreign land.

2.9.0.en: 10 "Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest: because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction. 11 If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.

2.9.1.en: Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your rest.

2.9.2.en: Because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction. [10]

2.9.3.en: In bitterness he calls them to arise and depart into captivity, for the fruit of their uncleanness and the sore destruction has come upon them! The divine sentence of chastening has been pronounced upon them, for since they robbed the rights of the people by their temporal authority, their possessions are taken from them by force, and the Promised Land is no longer a place of rest for them.

2.9.4.en: There comes upon them what came upon their fathers who murmured against God in the wilderness again and again. As it is written in the Psalm: "Forty years long was I grieved with this generation, and said, It is a people that do err in their heart, and they have not known my ways: unto whom I sware in my wrath that they should not enter into my rest" (Ps 95:10-11).

2.9.5.en: It does not stop at their being driven out of the Promised Land, but "because it is polluted, it shall destroy you, even with a sore destruction": the secret of their destruction is not the military strength of the enemy who takes them captive, but their own destructive uncleanness. Therefore Scripture charges us: "having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust" (2 Pet 1:4), "Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world" (Jas 1:27).

2.9.6.en: The prophet calls them to arise from the state of sin, so that they may enjoy true rest and destruction may not come upon them.

2.9.7.en: * Would that he who is unable to fly like the eagle might fly like a sparrow. He who is not able to fly to heaven, let him fly to those mountains. Would that he might fly before the valleys, these which are quickly destroyed by the waters. Let him cross over the mountains. The cousin of Abraham crossed over the mountains of Zoar (Segor) and was saved (Gen 19:12-29). But Lot's wife could not climb them, for she looked back in a womanly way and lost her salvation (Gen 19:26). The Lord says by the prophet Micah: "Draw near to the everlasting mountains, go up from here, for there is no rest for you in them because of uncleanness. By corruption ye are corrupted, ye suffer expulsion." He says: "Let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains" (Mt 24:16). There is mount Zion, and so the city of peace Jerusalem, built not of earthly stones but of living stones, by an innumerable company of angels and the church of the firstborn and the spirits of just men made perfect, and by the God of the righteous who spoke by blood better than Abel (Heb 12:24). For one cried out for vengeance (Gen 14:10) and the other for forgiveness. One reproves his brother's sin, and the other forgives the sin of the world. One proclaims a crime and the other covers a crime, as it is written: "Blessed are they whose sins are covered" (Ps 32:1) LXX.

2.9.8.en: St. Ambrose * "In the Lord put I my trust: how say ye to my soul, Flee as a bird to your mountain?" (Ps 11:1) LXX. A violent enemy! He tempted the Lord the Savior in the wilderness, and now he seeks the believers, he seeks each one of them to leave the land of Judaea and dwell in a wilderness barren of virtues, so that he may crush them there very easily. Even the counsel itself (which he offers) is crafty. It is not an advice that (the believer) take the wings of a dove, the gentle, simple, tame bird, a bird of which they say that it has never any malice, the one which was offered in the temple for the Lord (Lk 2:24), but (he counsels them to take) the wings of a sparrow, a chattering (chirping), roving bird, which becomes a stranger to its mate after the young emerge from the eggs.

2.9.9.en: St. Jerome If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying:

2.10.0.en: I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people! [11]

2.10.1.en: The prophet attacked their acceptance of the false prophets who, for the sake of their material or social benefit, overlook the truth and flatter the oppressors and cover up wrong. For this reason the Apostle says: "For if I yet pleased men, I should not be the servant of Christ" (Gal 1:10).

2.10.2.en: If someone came to speak to them of wine and strong drink, the oppressors would find in his talk what qualifies him to be a prophet to them, speaking to them of what they desire. They do not want a true prophet who utters the word of God, because for them it is disgrace and shame.

2.10.3.en: They want wicked prophets who agree with them in their evils, of whom it is said: "When thou sawest a thief, then thou consentedst with him, and hast been partaker with adulterers. Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit" (Ps 50:18-19).

2.10.4.en: Perhaps he is pointing here to the false prophets who, instead of becoming drunk with the love of God and being occupied with the divine commandment, are occupied with the licentious feasts held by the rich, and fall into drunkenness, which robs them of their balance and turns them aside from their mission.

2.10.5.en: * No sooner had they begun to plunge into the abyss of excess and deviate from the natural senses than they surrendered their souls to captivity under the tyrant of corrupt drunkenness.

2.10.6.en: They resemble a ship without ballast to keep its balance, therefore it is said: [Woe unto them that rise up early in the morning, that they may follow strong drink] (cf. Isa 5:11). They do not satisfy a need, nor do they wait for the desire to subside, but this is their work, to be drunk continually. Therefore it is said: "that they may follow strong drink."

2.11.0.en: 12 "I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as the flock in the midst of their fold: they shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men. 13 The breaker is come up before them: they have broken up, and have passed through the gate, and are gone out by it: and their king shall pass before them, and the LORD on the head of them."

2.11.1.en: As is the habit of the prophets, after the threat of chastening and before its coming, they open the door of hope so that they may perceive the surpassing mercy of God. For when He chastens, it is in order to gather them to Himself, and to give them more than they ask and above what they seek.

2.11.2.en: I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee.

2.11.3.en: I will surely gather the remnant of Israel.

2.11.4.en: I will put them together as the sheep of the fold, as the flock in the midst of their fold: they shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men. [12]

2.11.5.en: Some scholars see in these two statements [12-13] a prophecy of the return from captivity in the near future, and of the enjoyment of freedom from the captivity of sin by the coming of the Messiah, the Savior of the world.

2.11.6.en: A wonderful prophecy of two great events: the first, the return of Israel from the Babylonian captivity, and the second, the gathering together of the host of believers at the coming of the Lord Christ, who walks at their head as the firstborn from the dead and the heavenly head of the Church.

2.11.7.en: Others see that these two statements are the prophecy of the false, deceiving prophets that the captivity would end quickly and the return would be accomplished at once; this prophecy was not fulfilled.

2.11.8.en: If they were scattered because of their evil, then after chastening them He gathers them together, not as two divided kingdoms, but as one people and one kingdom, and calls all of them "Jacob." He will gather the holy remnant who clung to the Lord during the captivity and returned to Him, and they will become the sheep of His rational flock.

2.11.9.en: "They shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men," or they make a commotion because of the great number, where the Lord Christ, the Good Shepherd, gathers His people from all nations: "that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad" (Jn 11:52). As He says: "And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd" (Jn 10:16).

2.11.10.en: The breaker is come up before them.

2.12.0.en: They have broken up, and have passed through the gate, and are gone out by it: and their king shall pass before them, and the LORD on the head of them. [13]

2.12.1.en: Who is this breaker who breaks through the gate and passes through it, and goes out and brings out his people with him, but the Lord Christ, who broke death; He put it to death by His death. He brought His people through the gate of Hades and entered with them into His Paradise, granting them the spirit of victory over the last enemy, which is death?

2.12.2.en: He became the firstborn from the dead and raised us with Him! He came out of the tomb and carried its gate, as Samson took the doors of the gate of the city and the two posts and pulled them up, bar and all, and put them upon his shoulders and went out (Judg 16:3).

2.12.3.en: Some see that the breaker here is St. John the Baptist, who came in the spirit of Elijah to prepare the way before the King of kings, the Savior of the world, for he opened the door by proclaiming repentance and calling to a meeting with the Lamb of God who bears the sin of the world.

2.12.4.en: In the midst of the darkness the Savior advances, the light of the world, to shine with His light and scatter the darkness. He is called here the breaker, that is, the remover of obstacles and the opener of the way toward eternity. He opens the door wide so that every believer may find in it hope to enter in and go out under His leadership.

2.12.5.en: * He who enters must not remain in the same state in which he entered, but must go to the pasture, so that the entering is the beginning of the perfection of graces: "shall go in and out, and find pasture" (Jn 10:9). He who enters is confined within the limits of the world, but he who continues to walk, as one passing beyond created things, reckoning what is seen as nothing, finds pasture above the heavens, and feeds on the word of God, saying: "The Lord is my shepherd (He feeds me); I shall not want" (Ps 23:1) LXX. But this entering cannot be accomplished except by Christ, as followed: "and the LORD on the head of them."

2.12.7.en: Let Your Spirit work in me!
